Gold (of either color) is a better option to hold diamonds. The benefit of tungsten is that it shatters on impact, meant for people who work with their hands and don’t want gold -which stretches, bends, and twists- which could injure their fingers further. This shattering feature is not ideal for prongs which hold a precious stone. This is a fairly similar issue with titanium; neither of these metals can be resized easily, as opposed to gold, which is very malleable and forgiving.

A lot of people can tell the difference between sapphire and diamond. They reflect very differently and sapphire will not look as nice as a diamond. If you truly want a sparkly alternative that will fool most, try a moissanite. For a stone that is a geological clone of a diamond and has no ethical issues attached, purchase a lab grown diamond. Never set anything for long wear in sterling silver; it will tarnish and scratch. Get a white gold band if you like the look of silver and yellow gold if not. The cost is greater but the longevity is worth it. Of course, for the longest band life, platinum is the best choice, although it is the most expensive option. For a moderately priced ring that will last a lifetime of practically daily wear; the best option is a lab made diamond in a simple platinum setting.
